stories.title: At COP31, PM Shehbaz calls for grant-based finance, resilience funding for climate-vulnerable countries
summary: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday called for grant-based finance and improved resilience and adaptation funds for climate-vulnerable countries at COP31, being held in Turkiye’s Antalya.
The prime minister also held several bilateral conversations with world leaders and international organisations on the sidelines of the summit on Wednesday.
On Wednesday, the UN chief told world leaders at the summit that the slow international response to climate change so far had placed the world on a path to destruction.

stories.title: 'Significant evidence' of placer gold in Punjab rivers, says CM Maryam at minerals investment forum
summary: She was speaking at the Pakistan Minerals Investment Forum in Islamabad, an initiative aimed at harnessing the country’s mineral resources and attracting domestic and foreign investment in the mining sector.
Dar said Balochistan was central to Pakistan’s mineral future, adding that the development of its resources should contribute meaningfully to the provincial economy and the well-being of its people.

The Reko Diq copper-gold project in Balochistan is one of Pakistan’s most ambitious mining ventures, with significant potential to boost the country’s mineral wealth through the extraction of gold and copper.

stories.title: China says US using spy claims to justify technology 'blockade'
summary: The Nvidia boss has spent years lobbying against curbs on sales of advanced chips to China.
US President Donald Trump last year cleared Nvidia’s H200 chips for export there over objections from hawks in both parties who fear Beijing winning the race to dominate in AI technology.
China has dismissed the claims about spying on Huang as “groundless speculation” and “an attempt to smear China”.

stories.title: Democrats seek bipartisan action to curb Trump’s immigration drive
summary: WASHINGTON: Democratic lawmakers have called for a bipartisan immigration deal, seeking changes to President Donald Trump’s enforcement policies and legal status for long-settled immigrants.

The lawmakers’ appeal for federal legislation coincided with efforts by Democratic state and local administrations to narrow the role of their police and detention agencies in enforcing federal civil immigration rules.

Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger has ordered state law-enforcement agencies to end their agreements with ICE under the 287(g) programme, which authorises participating local and state officers to carry out specified immigration enforcement duties.

stories.title: Israeli strike kills 6 at southern Gaza hospital: civil defence
summary: An Israeli strike killed six people and wounded around 20 at Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, a civil defence official told AFP on Thursday.
The Israeli military confirmed the strike.

On Tuesday, Israeli forces killed seven people, including a 13-year-old boy, in the Gaza Strip, according to local emergency services, while the Israeli military claimed it had targeted “military operatives”.

stories.title: Debutant Saqib Khan takes seven as Pakistan restrict Sri Lanka to slender lead
summary: Debutant fast bowler Saqib Khan produced a remarkable seven-wicket haul as Pakistan restricted Sri Lanka to a slender 12-run first-innings lead on the fourth day of the opening Test at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Thursday.

Saqib finished with outstanding figures of seven for 130 in 34 overs, equalling the record for the most wickets by a Pakistani bowler on Test debut and becoming only the fourth player from the country to claim a seven-wicket haul in his first Test innings.
His sustained accuracy and ability to extract assistance from the surface ensured Sri Lanka could not turn their strong position into a commanding first-innings lead.

stories.title: US marine guard appears to rebuke Hegseth's delegation at Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
summary: A US Army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier appeared to rebuke Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth’s delegation on Wednesday after laughter could be heard as they climbed the steps of the solemn site, according to a video of the incident.
Hegseth, his wife and senior aides could be seen taking pictures and speaking to each other on the steps of the memorial at Arlington National Cemetery following a Veterans Day event.
Democrats who won control of both chambers of Congress last week have promised to investigate Hegseth for his stewardship of the US military and have not ruled out another impeachment effort.

stories.title: Trump to flex muscles on Asia tour after midterms losses
summary: After his party suffered a midterms hammering, President Donald Trump faces a new challenge: proving he is still the boss of US foreign policy on the global stage.

With Trump politically hamstrung as he enters the remaining two-year ‘lame duck’ period of his White House tenure, world leaders may be quietly wondering how to leverage the new balance of power in Washington.
High-profile meeting Trump relishes dramatic gestures and foreign policy provides an ideal arena for high-profile meetings, such as with Chinese and Russian leaders Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

stories.title: War, poverty, repression stalk Yemen's ancient capital
summary: Beset by poverty, war and repression, the residents of Yemen’s ancient capital Sanaa, under Houthi control for over a decade, struggle to survive.
Alongside the struggle to secure basic necessities, residents of Sanaa complain of constant power cuts.
Bilqis Abu-Osba, a former political science lecturer at Sanaa University who now lives outside the city, said dropouts have become endemic.

stories.title: Peshawar High Court upholds posting of higher education dept officer as DG law
summary: The petitioners, including Aya Khan and five other former employees of the directorate of law, had requested the court to declare illegal the appointment of Ghulam Ali as DG (law and human rights) on Dec 13, 2023.
The lawyer added that the government, in violation of those rules, issued the impugned notification on Dec 13, 2023, whereby Ghulam Ali was posted as the DG.

According to them, the date when Ghulam Ali was posted, the subsequent restriction prescribing that the post of DG be filled by transfer from among officers of PAS, PCS or PMS had not yet been introduced through the said amendment.

stories.title: KP health directorate told to shift remaining offices from old Fata Secretariat
summary: Officials said the DGHS office had already informed the health adviser and secretary about the situation, requesting their intervention to resolve the matter, as the move could bring health-related activities in the province to a standstill.

They said the directorate had already vacated 20 rooms, including halls, for the ADS and had been directed to vacate the remaining offices and shift to a dilapidated building belonging to the livestock and dairy development department.
They said the DGHS was an implementing arm of the health department’s secretariat and oversaw health services across the province, including those provided by more than 2,600 hospitals.

stories.title: President, PM condole martyrdom of 10 policemen in Kohat, vow to continue fight against terrorism
summary: President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday expressed grief over the martyrdom of 10 police personnel in a terrorist attack on a police team in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kohat district.

Calling them national heroes, he said the brave officers and personnel of the provincial police force had set an example of devotion to duty and courage by laying down their lives for the peace and security of the country.

The prime minister further said the courage and steadfastness shown by police personnel and other law enforcement agencies in the fight against terrorism were commendable, adding that the entire nation stood shoulder to shoulder with the country’s security forces.

stories.title: Faryal Talpur in Lahore to ‘activate PPP in Punjab’
summary: LAHORE: Faryal Talpur, the central head of the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Women’s Wing, arrived in Lahore for a four-day visit on Wednesday.
From the airport, Faryal Talpur proceeded directly to Bilawal House, Lahore, where she will hold key meetings with party leaders and office-bearers during her stay.
Discussions with party leaders and female office-bearers will cover the wing’ organisational matters and the future political strategy.

stories.title: Power shutdown at Dhabeji to cause Karachi-wide water shortage tomorrow
summary: According to a KWSC spokesperson, KE has formally notified the water utility of the scheduled power shutdown. “Electricity supply to Dhabeji Grid Station will remain suspended on Nov 13 for annual maintenance,” he said.
During this period, only three pumps at Dhabeji would remain non-operational, resulting in a partial disruption of water supply to Landhi, Korangi, Malir and Shah Faisal.
Meanwhile, a KE spokesperson said the scheduled maintenance shutdown at Dhabeji Grid Station would take place on Friday and that advance notice had been shared with the KWSC.

stories.title: Chiniot man booked for keeping pet dog without NOC after it mauls two
summary: CHINIOT: The City police have registered a case against a citizen after his pet dog injured two persons and booked him for keeping the dog without a no objection certificate (NOC) from the Chiniot municipal committee.

As per details, on the complaint of Municipal Committee Enforcement Inspector Muhammad Saleem, the City police registered the case stating that suspect Nazim Ali, a resident of Mohallah Baqir Wali of Chiniot, was keeping a pet dog in his house without an NOC.
ACCIDENT: A youth was critically injured after being hit by a Punjab government’s electric bus, which was allegedly plying on the wrong side of the Chiniot-Sargodha Road.

stories.title: Karachi's Malir Development Authority under FIA scrutiny after two held over fake bank challans
summary: The FIA also recovered Rs20 million in cash and stamps bearing the names of different banks during the operation, pointing to an alleged network involved in generating and using fake bank challans to facilitate financial fraud.
Agency claims to have recovered Rs20m in cash and stamps bearing names of different banks during raid “The recovered cash is believed to have been generated through these alleged illegal activities.
The fresh arrests have raised further questions about the possible involvement of other officials within the MDA and individuals outside the authority in the alleged fraud.

stories.title: PPP has no objection to creation of new provinces, except in Sindh: CM Murad
summary: THATTA: Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah said on Wednesday that, except for Sindh, the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) had no objection to the creation of new provinces in other parts of the country if their people so desired.
He made it clear that the division of Sindh was “neither legally nor politically acceptable, as the people of the province had repeatedly rejected the idea through their elected representatives”.
The chief minister said the people of Sindh had repeatedly expressed their opposition to the division of the province through their elected representatives.

stories.title: Drug trafficking network busted, 20 Nigerians arrested in Islamabad, Rawalpindi
summary: RAWALPINDI: The Anti-Narcotics Force (ANF) busted an international drug trafficking network targeting youth in twin cities, arrested 20 Nigerian nationals, and recovered 4.432kg of narcotics during a crackdown in Islamabad and Rawalpindi.

Acting on credible intelligence, ANF conducted a coordinated intelligence-based operation at various locations across the twin cities, resulting in the arrest of 20 Nigerians allegedly involved in drug trafficking and recovered 4.43kg of narcotics.

These operations demonstrate ANF’s professional capabilities, operational effectiveness and unwavering commitment to dismantling organised drug trafficking networks involved in the illicit transportation and distribution of narcotics.

stories.title: Pakistan Railways joins hands with LDA to earn revenue from its prime properties
summary: LAHORE: The Pakistan Railways (PR) has joined hands with the Lahore Development Authority (LDA) for a business plan to earn the maximum revenue from its prime commercial properties in the city, including one situated near the Lahore Railway Station.

We requested the LDA to prepare a viable business plan that can help us earn the optimum revenue through auction of leasing rights and other business interventions,” said a senior railways official while talking to Dawn on Tuesday.
Minister for Railways Hanif Abbasi confirmed the development, terming it a government-to-government joint venture. “We have placed our properties before the LDA in a recent meeting.

stories.title: Capital Development Authority chief orders resolution of Park Enclave issues
summary: According to the press release, residents of Park Enclave placed before Chairman CDA their issues relating to the repair of boundary wall, sanitation system, public parks, security, electricity supply in Park Enclave Phase-II and III and other basic facilities.

Mr Ashraf directed the relevant department to improve the sanitation system in Park Enclave under modern solid waste management services, and that work be carried out regarding the repair of a boundary wall to improve security in Phase I.

Mr Ashraf directed the relevant wing to immediately complete the remaining development work in Phase-III and said that issues related to sewage, water supply and up-gradation of parks should also be resolved on a priority basis.

stories.title: Medical superintendent, two doctors in Faisalabad suspended on LHC orders
summary: TOBA TEK SINGH: On the direction of the Lahore High Court (LHC), the secretary of the Punjab specialised healthcare and medical education department has suspended the medical superintendent of Faisalabad Allied Hospital II (former DHQ Hospital) along with two other doctors.
ACCIDENT: A biker was killed after a trailer hit his motorcycle near the Parco oil depot on Chak Jhumra Road in Faisalabad on Wednesday evening.
The injured biker was being shifted to the Allied Hospital but he succumbed to his injuries on the way.

For security reasons, which must be recorded in writing, the authority may inspect and integrate public and private CCTV cameras and fibre-optic networks without compromising citizens’ privacy, to improve digital surveillance and ensure maximum public security.
The authority will issue directives regarding integration and compliance under the ordinance.

stories.title: BJP accuses Sonia Gandhi of ‘camouflaging Congress sins’ in memoir
summary: NEW DELHI: India’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party has accused opposition leader Sonia Gandhi of whitewashing historical wrongs by her Congress party in a memoir, sparking a new faceoff between the two sides ahead of key state elections.
Congress party leaders have in turn accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s BJP of trying to create a spectacle and give the book a “political spin”.
Kesavan cited the anti-Sikh riots of 1984 which erupted after then-prime minister and Sonia’s mother-in-law Indira Gandhi was assassinated by Sikh bodyguards.

summary: He said the transition of the Makkah Joint Defence Alliance into the practical implementation phase of its collective defence commitments would require measures to ensure the rapid deployment of agreed forces and military capabilities inside Saudi Arabia.
For Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, the trilateral pact is built on their Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement signed in September 2025.
Pakistan had also expanded its military and security cooperation with the kingdom, deploying about 8,000 troops, fighter jets, drones and an air-defence system to Saudi Arabia, according to Reuters.

stories.title: PSX sheds 1,492 points as selling hits heavyweights
summary: The benchmark KSE-100 Index of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) traded sharply lower at midday on Thursday, losing 1,492.16 points, or 0.83 per cent, to stand at 177,591.64.
The index had touched an intraday high of 180,310.44 earlier in the session before selling pressure pulled it down.
Trading volume in the index reached 164.54 million shares, while the value of shares traded stood at Rs15.22 billion.

summary: Justice Mandokhail also underscored that the judicial oath demanded impartiality, integrity and unwavering adherence to the Constitution and the law, without fear, favour or external influence.
Paying tribute to Justice Mandokhail, Chief Justice Afridi lauded his distinguished judicial career and commitment to the administration of justice.
He particularly highlighted Justice Mandokhail’s efforts to strengthen the district judiciary and judicial infrastructure during his tenure as chief justice of the Balochistan High Court.

stories.title: Pakistan courts global investors at Minerals Investment Forum as provinces outline opportunities
summary: While addressing the forum, Deputy Prime Minister (DPM) and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar highlighted Pakistan's vast mineral resources and efforts to diversify its export base, saying the country stood at a pivotal juncture in its economic journey.

The deputy prime minister described Balochistan as vital to Pakistan's mineral future, noting that the global transition to clean energy was driving demand for copper and creating new opportunities for mineral exploration in the country.
The chief minister also highlighted efforts to increase the value of pink salt exports, saying the mineral had previously been exported in raw form, limiting Pakistan's earnings.

Before he could mend things, a Punjab minister spoiled the matter by launching a verbal attack on us,” he said, adding that he had not directly levelled corruption allegations against the chief minister.

stories.title: Mississippi Democrat flips US Senate seat in stunning upset
summary: In a historic upset, Democrat Scott Colom has won his US Senate race in traditionally conservative Mississippi, networks projected on Wednesday, making him the first African American elected to the chamber from the southern state in more than 140 years.

He wanted us to get it the Mississippi way." Colom's win in the Deep South adds sting to the stunning rebuke of President Donald Trump as voters around the country shunned his Republican Party, even in states that had not sent a Democrat to Washington in decades.
I knew it from the moment I met him." Colom is set to become the first Democratic senator from Mississippi in nearly 40 years.

stories.title: Punjab govt insists smog ‘not a political issue’ as Lahore, New Delhi gasp for air
summary: Meanwhile, the toxic smog in second-placed New Delhi — with an AQI reading of 248 on Wednesday — was so severe this week that air pollution monitors in the country were overwhelmed after pollutant concentrations exceeded the upper measurement limits on their instruments.

On Wednesday, the Punjab Environment Protection Agency (EPA) — in its assessment for the Diwali period — found that pollution-laden air from India travelled deep into Punjab, contributing to increased particulate matter (PM) concentrations.
Readings from Punjab’s air quality monitoring network showed a marked geographical variation in particulate pollution across Lahore.

stories.title: Son says South Korea players resolve internal divisions
summary: Son Heung-min and four other South Korean players said Thursday they had put their differences aside after reports of bitter internal divisions at the heart of the national team.
South Korean football has been mired in controversy since their hugely disappointing exit in the group stage of the World Cup, after which unpopular coach Hong Myung-bo quit.
"First of all we would like to sincerely apologise to the Korean public and football fans for the concern caused by recent reports concerning the national team," the statement said.

stories.title: Saqib Khan (7-130) rips through Sri Lanka batting in Rawalpindi Test
summary: Young fast bowler Saqib Khan ripped through Sri Lanka's batting line-up on the fourth morning to claim a seven-wicket haul, but the visitors secured a narrow 12-run first-innings lead in the opening Test against Pakistan on Thursday.
Pakistan quickly turned the pressure on the visitors, with Saqib breaking the stand by dismissing de Silva for 167 before removing Kusal for 119 as Sri Lanka lost two wickets for eight runs.

De Silva (167 not out) and Mendis (117 not out) put together 249 runs for the fifth-wicket unbroken stand to enable Sri Lanka to reach 404-4 in 102 overs in their first innings as bad light hastened the stumps.

stories.title: Sindh to unlock mineral wealth through scientific exploration, responsible mining
summary: Presiding over a meeting at the CM House, he reviewed Sindh’s coal and non-coal mineral resources, ongoing mining projects and opportunities for domestic and international investment.
The minister cited the Thar coal projects as examples of how mining could contribute to local development through jobs, education, healthcare, clean drinking water and community infrastructure.

The chief minister reaffirmed that the Sindh government would open up the province’s mineral resources, saying that coal and other minerals had enormous potential to drive industrialisation, strengthen energy security, create jobs and accelerate economic growth.

stories.title: 7.1m children vaccinated across Sindh in anti-polio drive
summary: KARACHI: Around 7.1 million children across the province have been vaccinated against polio during the recently concluded weeklong campaign, while routine immunisation activities continue in 121 union councils in seven districts of the metropolis.

EOC officials informed the meeting that over 98 per cent of the household vaccination target had been achieved during the campaign; over 2.3m children were vaccinated through household visits in Karachi.
The officials encouraged parents to complete their children’s routine immunisation and ensure that no vaccine dose is missed.
